title: Relative normalization in a dense open of a normal locally Noetherian scheme is trivial
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] all of whose stalks are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let V be an open subset dense in X. The canonical integral morphism from the relative normalization of X in V [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] to X is an isomorphism. X may be empty or disconnected.

source.place: Tags 0357 (normal components), 035I (relative normalization), 0AB1 (normal birational comparison), applied componentwise to a dense open

proof.text: The domain stalks imply reduced stalks and hence reducedness of X. The dense open immersion V into X is dominant, and therefore scheme-theoretically dominant. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.app_injective gives injectivity of restriction on every open. Thus the algebra map from sections on an affine U to their integral closure in sections on V intersect U is injective.

Apply [lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section] to each element of this integral closure. It is integral by its subtype membership, and the extension lemma supplies an element of the sections on U with the same restriction. Subtype.ext identifies the two integral-closure elements. The algebra map to the integral closure is therefore surjective as well.

On an affine U, Mathlib Hom.fromNormalization_app expresses the section map of the canonical normalization morphism as the bijective algebra map followed by the inverse normalizationObjIso. RingEquiv.ofBijective makes the algebra map a ring isomorphism, so this section map is an isomorphism. The normalization morphism is integral, hence affine; isIso_morphismRestrict_iff_isIso_app proves that its restriction over U is an isomorphism. Finally apply target locality for isomorphisms to the affine open cover iSup_affineOpens_eq_top. This includes empty affine opens and the empty scheme.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0357, 035I and 0AB1; integral-section extension plus Mathlib affine normalization and target locality

mathlib_searches.query: A normal locally Noetherian scheme is its relative normalization in any dense open subscheme
The relative normalization of a locally Noetherian normal scheme in a dense open subscheme is an isomorphism
mathlib_searches.results: Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Normalization: instIsIsoToNormalizationOfIsIntegralHom, instIsIntegralNormalization, instIsIntegralHomFromNormalization, normalizationDesc. The first concerns toNormalization for an integral morphism, not fromNormalization of an open immersion; none states the result.
Only instIsIsoNormalizationPullbackOfSmooth: normalization commutes with smooth base change, not the required triviality statement.

Upstream isIso_fromNormalization_restrict and isIso_fromNormalization_app concern normalization in the function field of an integral scheme. They do not apply to possibly empty or disconnected normal schemes normalized in an arbitrary dense open. Read Mathlib normalization source and upstream complements; no exact match.

from.place: Integral-closure identification of the finite normal model in the trait-case step; normal schemes are determined by the common dense open

theorem isIso_fromNormalization_denseOpen
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hnormal : ∀ z : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk z))
    (V : X.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X)) :
    IsIso V.ι.fromNormalization
